segments.he: הרב הצדיק מבארדיטשוב ז"ל אמר שכשמגיע ימים נוראים דוקר לו בגבו "אז ער גאט ימים נוראים שטעחט אים דיא פליידע" ואמר מהרנ"ת ז"ל ע"ז מי שאין דוקר לו כמה צריך שידקור לו בגבו "דער וואס שטעכט אים ניט וויפול בארץ מים שוין שטעדין:
segments.en: Reb Mikheli of Tulchin, grandson of Moharan'as, said about communal prayer and its great virtue: it is accepted even if there are inferior members in the prayer — just as when one gives several coins together, even if there is an inferior coin among them it still passes. But if one gives only a single coin, it is examined carefully. So it is with communal prayer versus individual prayer. And Reb Mikheli lived in Tulchin and was very distinguished. He would study Torah publicly there, and after the prayer would stand with the other ardent members of our fellowship and speak with them of matters of the service of G-d. There were people there who were not of our fellowship and would speak idle words and news — disturbing our fellowship so they could not speak and study. They restrained themselves with all their strength from telling those people not to speak so loudly, so as not to come to a quarrel. Despite this they were so disturbed that they could not bear it — until one of our fellowship, Reb Shechin'a grandson of Moharan'as, said to Reb Mikheli: "I am going to tell them to stop disturbing us." Reb Mikheli answered: "Zog, zog!" [Say! Say!] And Reb Shechin'a thought he was being given permission to go tell them. Reb Mikheli completed his sentence: "Zog zikh — zog zikh!" [Tell yourself — say it to yourself!] When Reb Mikheli was in Eretz Yisroel and was at the grave of Rashbi and studied Zohar there, he said that he derived enormous pleasure from it — that he felt a completely different taste in the Zohar each time he studied it. But the taste he felt in the Zohar studied at the grave of Rashbi was wondrously far greater. He said about this: "It is good to drink from the tap itself." "S'iz gut tsi trunken fun tsapn." [At the root itself one feels a different taste.]
